newsitem.title: USA: AT&T enters mobile workforce market.
newsitem.headline: AT&T enters mobile workforce market.

text.p: AT&T Corp said on Wednesday it entered the mobile workforce communications market with a private network service allowing workers to communicate and use their company's data networks from remote locations.

The service is AT&T's first offering in a niche market of 20 million U.S. salespeople, delivery, security and real estate staff which Geotek Communications Inc Nextel Communications Inc are already aiming for.
The service will allow mobile workers with laptops to use their company's computer systems with Microsoft Corp Windows 95 software and a mobile automation platform.
The system architecture used was designed by Adaptive Strategies Inc, AT&T said.

The service allows the mobile worker toll-free connection to his company's database at the click of a mouse, and send or receive information, and transfer E-mail messages. AT&T will provide all the customer support.
The cost is $395 per user per month, plus a one-time activation charge dependent on the number of users.
